title: Mittag-Leffler passes to quotients and makes lim exact (Stacks 02N1 (2), (3))
statement: Let $0\to(A_i)\xrightarrow{(u_i)}(B_i)\xrightarrow{(v_i)}(C_i)\to0$ be a short exact sequence of inverse systems of abelian groups indexed by $i\ge1$ [def-weil-inverse-system]: $(u_i)$ and $(v_i)$ are morphisms of inverse systems (they commute with the transition maps) and $0\to A_i\xrightarrow{u_i}B_i\xrightarrow{v_i}C_i\to0$ is exact for every $i$. For an inverse system $(M_i)$ let $\varprojlim_iM_i=\{(x_i)\in\prod_iM_i:x_{i+1}\mapsto x_i\text{ for all }i\}$, so that $(v_i)$ induces $\varprojlim v_i:\varprojlim_iB_i\to\varprojlim_iC_i$, $(x_i)\mapsto(v_i(x_i))$. Then: (2) if $(B_i)$ is ML [def-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-system], then $(C_i)$ is ML; (3) if $(A_i)$ is ML, then $\varprojlim v_i$ is surjective, so that $0\to\varprojlim_iA_i\to\varprojlim_iB_i\to\varprojlim_iC_i\to0$ is exact.

proof.text: Notation. Write $a_i:A_{i+1}\to A_i$, $b_i:B_{i+1}\to B_i$, $t_i:C_{i+1}\to C_i$ for the transition maps and $a_{k,i},b_{k,i},t_{k,i}$ ($k\ge i$) for their composites $A_k\to A_i$, $B_k\to B_i$, $C_k\to C_i$ [def-weil-inverse-system], so that $b_{k,i}=b_{j,i}\circ b_{k,j}$ for $k\ge j\ge i$, and likewise for $a$ and $t$. Since $u$ and $v$ are morphisms of inverse systems, $b_i\circ u_{i+1}=u_i\circ a_i$ and $t_i\circ v_{i+1}=v_i\circ b_i$; composing these squares $k-i$ times gives $b_{k,i}\circ u_k=u_i\circ a_{k,i}$ and $t_{k,i}\circ v_k=v_i\circ b_{k,i}$ for all $k\ge i$ (induction on $k-i$). Exactness of $0\to A_i\to B_i\to C_i\to0$ means: $u_i$ is injective, $v_i$ is surjective and $\ker v_i=u_i(A_i)$. Also, if $(x_i)\in\varprojlim_iM_i$ for an inverse system $(M_i)$ with composites $m_{k,i}$, then $m_{k,i}(x_k)=x_i$ for all $k\ge i$ (induction on $k-i$).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 0598 (lemma-ML-exact-sequence, algebra.tex lines 20770--20815), proof (the notation $\varphi_{ji}$, $f_i$, $g_i$ there)

proof.text: Part (2). Assume $(B_i)$ is ML [def-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-system] and fix $i\ge1$; let $c=c(i)\ge i$ be such that $b_{k,i}(B_k)=b_{c,i}(B_c)$ for all $k\ge c$. For every $k\ge i$, since $v_k$ is surjective and $t_{k,i}\circ v_k=v_i\circ b_{k,i}$ (Step 1), $t_{k,i}(C_k)=t_{k,i}(v_k(B_k))=v_i(b_{k,i}(B_k))$. Hence for $k\ge c$: $t_{k,i}(C_k)=v_i(b_{k,i}(B_k))=v_i(b_{c,i}(B_c))=t_{c,i}(C_c)$. So the same $c(i)$ witnesses the ML condition for $(C_i)$ at $i$, and $(C_i)$ is ML [def-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-system].

proof.text: Part (3), the fibres. Assume $(A_i)$ is ML and let $(c_i)\in\varprojlim_iC_i$. For $i\ge1$ put $E_i=v_i^{-1}(c_i)\subseteq B_i$; it is nonempty since $v_i$ is surjective. For $k\ge i$ and $e\in E_k$, $v_i(b_{k,i}(e))=t_{k,i}(v_k(e))=t_{k,i}(c_k)=c_i$ (Step 1), so $b_{k,i}(E_k)\subseteq E_i$. Hence the restrictions $b_i|_{E_{i+1}}:E_{i+1}\to E_i$ make $(E_i)_{i\ge1}$ an inverse system of nonempty sets [def-weil-inverse-system] whose composites are the restrictions of the $b_{k,i}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 0598 (lemma-ML-exact-sequence, algebra.tex lines 20770--20815), proof, first paragraph (the sets $E_i=g_i^{-1}(c_i)$)

proof.text: Part (3), $(E_i)$ satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition for sets. Fix $i\ge1$ and let $j=c(i)\ge i$ be given by the ML condition for $(A_i)$ [def-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-system]: $a_{k,i}(A_k)=a_{j,i}(A_j)$ for all $k\ge j$. We claim $b_{k,i}(E_k)=b_{j,i}(E_j)$ for all $k\ge j$. The inclusion $\subseteq$: $b_{k,i}(E_k)=b_{j,i}(b_{k,j}(E_k))\subseteq b_{j,i}(E_j)$ by Step 3. For $\supseteq$, let $e_j\in E_j$. Choose any $e'_k\in E_k$ (Step 3) and put $e'_j=b_{k,j}(e'_k)\in E_j$. Then $v_j(e_j-e'_j)=c_j-c_j=0$, so $e_j-e'_j=u_j(\alpha)$ for some $\alpha\in A_j$ (exactness at $B_j$). As $a_{j,i}(\alpha)\in a_{j,i}(A_j)=a_{k,i}(A_k)$, there is $\beta\in A_k$ with $a_{k,i}(\beta)=a_{j,i}(\alpha)$. Put $x_k=e'_k+u_k(\beta)$; then $v_k(x_k)=v_k(e'_k)=c_k$, so $x_k\in E_k$, and by Step 1 $b_{k,i}(x_k)=b_{j,i}(b_{k,j}(e'_k))+u_i(a_{k,i}(\beta))=b_{j,i}(e'_j)+u_i(a_{j,i}(\alpha))=b_{j,i}(e'_j)+b_{j,i}(u_j(\alpha))=b_{j,i}(e'_j+e_j-e'_j)=b_{j,i}(e_j)$. So $b_{j,i}(e_j)\in b_{k,i}(E_k)$, proving the claim. Thus $(E_i)$, with $c(i)$ taken from $(A_i)$, satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition of [lem-weil-pbc-ml-sets-tower-limit-nonempty].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 0598 (lemma-ML-exact-sequence, algebra.tex lines 20770--20815), proof, second paragraph (the claim $\varphi_{ki}(E_k)=\varphi_{ji}(E_j)$ for $k\ge j$)

proof.text: Part (3), surjectivity of $\varprojlim v_i$. By Steps 3 and 4, $(E_i)$ is an inverse system of nonempty sets satisfying the Mittag-Leffler condition, so its limit is nonempty [lem-weil-pbc-ml-sets-tower-limit-nonempty]: there are $e_i\in E_i$ ($i\ge1$) with $b_i(e_{i+1})=e_i$ for all $i$. Then $(e_i)\in\varprojlim_iB_i$ and $(\varprojlim v_i)((e_i))=(v_i(e_i))=(c_i)$. As $(c_i)\in\varprojlim_iC_i$ was arbitrary, $\varprojlim v_i$ is surjective.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 0598 (lemma-ML-exact-sequence, algebra.tex lines 20770--20815), proof, first paragraph (Lemma 0597 applied to $(E_i)$)

proof.text: Part (3), exactness of the limit sequence. Abelian groups are $\mathbf Z$-modules and homomorphisms are $\mathbf Z$-linear; with $R=\mathbf Z$, $(K_n)=(A_i)$, $(B_n)=(B_i)$, $(C_n)=(C_i)$, the first assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-tower-limit-exact-surjective-kernels] (b) (whose limits are the same sets of compatible sequences as here) gives the exactness of $0\to\varprojlim_iA_i\xrightarrow{\varprojlim u_i}\varprojlim_iB_i\xrightarrow{\varprojlim v_i}\varprojlim_iC_i$, with no hypothesis on $(A_i)$. Together with Step 5, $0\to\varprojlim_iA_i\to\varprojlim_iB_i\to\varprojlim_iC_i\to0$ is exact when $(A_i)$ is ML.
